description:
Maintainer's ask, 2026-08-13, straight out of dogfooding: `bn sync` hung (bd-95p)
and there was NO supported way to bounce the daemon. Had to `pkill -f "bn daemon
run"` and let the next command autostart one. Cannot expect a user to reach for
pkill to recover their own tracker lah.

Today `bn daemon --help` offers exactly one thing:

    Commands:
      run   Run the daemon in the foreground (internal)

The good news: NOTHING new needs inventing. The whole mechanism is already
written and already cross-platform in
crates/kopi-beans/src/surface/ipc/client.rs — it is just PRIVATE, so only the
IPC retry path can reach it, never a user:

  * `kill_daemon_forcefully(pid, socket)` (:1162 unix, :1221 windows) —
    SIGTERM, wait 3s for the socket to go away, escalate to SIGKILL, wait 2s
    more, then remove `daemon.sock` + `daemon.meta.json` as last resort.
    Windows arm has no SIGTERM so it terminates directly, same cleanup.
    Missing process (ESRCH) is treated as success, which is what we want.
  * `try_restart_daemon_by_socket(socket)` (:1245) — reads the pid out of
    `daemon.meta.json`, else removes the stale socket.
  * `read_daemon_meta_at(socket)` (:132) -> `Option<DaemonInfo>` (version,
    protocol_version, pid, started_at_ms).
  * `socket_path()` (:119), and autostart already spawns `bn daemon run`
    (see `with_autostart_program`, :253).

So the job is plumbing, not design: expose a public stop/start, add the two
subcommands, wire the dispatch (cli.rs:363 `Command::Daemon` and the
`daemon_cmd_name` mapper at :621), and render like the existing
`render_daemon_info` ("daemon 0.1.4 (protocol 3, pid 4242)").

Behaviours that must be right:
  * `stop` when nothing is running = SUCCESS, exit 0, say so plainly. It must be
    idempotent — scripts and session-close hooks will call it blind.
  * `restart` must WAIT for the new daemon to be serving before returning, not
    just fire and hope. `wait_for_daemon_ready(expected_version)` (:329) already
    exists for exactly this.
  * `restart` with nothing running = just start one, not an error.
  * `--json` on both, same as every other command.
  * Report the OLD pid and the NEW pid on restart, so the user can see it really
    bounced.
  * Keep `bn daemon` hidden as it is now, but stop/restart are user-facing, so
    their help text must be written for a human.

Related: bd-95p (the `bn sync` hang that prompted this) and bd-cni (Windows: a
read autostarts a daemon that then blocks every write) — a working `stop` is the
recovery path for bd-cni too.
title: kopi-beans: add 'bn daemon stop' and 'bn daemon restart' (machinery exists, just not reachable)

description:
Falls out of bd-7ab / GH#1: `kopitiam check` and `kopitiam test` grew `--release`,
`--profile <NAME>` and `-- <CARGO_ARGS>` trailing passthrough, but the agent skill
does not mention any of them.

Matters more here than in a normal repo: CLAUDE.md's Build Rules mandate release
mode for this workspace, and the STANDARD RULE tells agents to reach for
`kopitiam check --compact` / `test --compact` instead of raw cargo. So an agent
following the skill as written will run DEV-profile checks on a release-only
workspace and report a dev-profile answer — the exact bug GH#1 was filed about,
reintroduced through the documentation.

HARD CONSTRAINT, per CLAUDE.md: `kopitiam_skill.md` is DETERMINISTICALLY generated
by `scripts/gen-kopitiam-skill.sh`. Fix the GENERATOR, never hand-edit the skill.

While in there, the same section still owes the code-navigation recipe
(tokens -> outline -> refs -> read) that CLAUDE.md says the skill currently lacks.
Worth doing in the same pass.
title: kopitiam_skill.md generator: teach it the new check/test --release, --profile and -- passthrough flags
